benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Jumped to about $105.2 on 8 Oct (Trading Economics $105.26, Investing.com $105.16-105.26), up roughly 5% on the day, as Hurricane Isaias forced US Gulf of Mexico producers to shut in about a quarter of oil output and the IMO recorded the highest weekly tanker-attack total in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began. Week-ago reuses 7 Oct (1 day prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week.

benchmarks.label: TTF gas
benchmarks.note: Rose to about €79.56 on 8 Oct (Trading Economics), up almost 2%, extending its multi-week high on continued risk to Hormuz LNG flows and Qatar's LNG-carrier positioning. Week-ago reuses 7 Oct (1 day prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week. Pre-crisis €32.00 is derived from RTÉ's figure of +€14.52 to €46.52 on 2 March.

benchmarks.label: Henry Hub
benchmarks.note: Climbed to $3.27 on 8 Oct (Trading Economics), a fifth straight session of gains, on expectations of cooler weather lifting heating demand. Week-ago reuses 7 Oct (1 day prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week; pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price is largely insulated.

note: Brent and WTI jumped about 5% to roughly $105 and $93 on 8 October as Hurricane Isaias forced Shell and Chevron to shut in about a quarter of US Gulf of Mexico oil output and evacuate staff from several platforms, while the IMO recorded the highest weekly tanker-attack total in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began. TTF and Henry Hub both rose.
